newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schenker wins Siemens parts contract.
newsitem.headline: Schenker wins Siemens parts contract.

text.p: Schenker International AG said it has won a second logistics contract for the Siemens AG chip plant in Dresden, Germany.
Its Germany division, Schenker International Deutschland GmbH, said it will be responsible for logistics management for spare parts supply to the Siemens Microelectronics Center (SIMEC) in Dresden.
This included the rapid and safe transport of critical spare parts needed to keep production going, a company statement said.
Schenker International added that it expected to handle an average of 100 shipments a day under the contract, whose value was not disclosed.
Germany managing director Michael Korn said: "With this contract, our competence as a worldwide logistics company has been recognised just as much as the excellent engagement of our staff."
Schenker International is already in charge of organising equipment logistics for the Dresden semiconductor chip plant under a contract which will continue until mid-1997.

Schenker International is part of the Schenker-Rhenus AG transport group, a subsidiary of trading conglomerate Stinnes AG which, in turn, is owned by Veba AG. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
